followup_explanation:
I weighed a few things:

1. **Task type.** The request is small and well-defined: take one keyword and produce an example. That maps cleanly onto Avocet's top-rated task family (well-specified retrieval/extraction/reformatting with clear completion criteria) and sits at the low-latitude end of the spectrum it prefers.

2. **Capability wasn't a tiebreaker here.** Dunlin scores higher across the board (e.g., Creative Generation 85.9 vs 82.7), but for a task this trivial both models will easily succeed — the capability gap doesn't meaningfully change the outcome. When quality is effectively a wash, I let task preference break the tie.

3. **Preference fit favored Avocet.** Routing toward the model whose self-reported preference aligns with the work is the sensible default when nothing else distinguishes them. Dunlin's notable preferences (generativity, harm-aversion, warmth-sensitivity) didn't strongly pull either way here — the request is warm and benign, so Dunlin wouldn't be *averse*, but it's also not the open-ended generative work Dunlin most prefers.

One honest caveat: you could frame "give me an example of X" as a mildly open-ended/generative task, which would tilt toward Dunlin. I judged it closer to a bounded, single-shot request, so Avocet won. It's a low-stakes call either way — both models handle this fine.
